nodes.label: Existing warehouse verification suite
nodes.rationale: unittest discovery covers incremental desktop refresh, cache responsibilities, atomic persistence, multi-location comparison/upload, shelf address lookup, and legacy database paths.

nodes.label: Complete location-set web update
nodes.rationale: LocationUpdate carries all local locations including exception placements; an empty set clears website locations. WebsiteUploader owns connection, product identity checks, selection, saving, and verification; location-only updates preserve stock.

nodes.label: WarehouseDatabase persistence facade
nodes.rationale: Composes schema, models, catalog, shelves, inventory, and exceptions domain operations into the database facade.

nodes.label: Browse Shelves
nodes.rationale: Shows saved shelves and unsaved Shelf Designer previews with distinct committed/uncommitted summaries; browsing does not change assignments.

nodes.label: Primal Queue / Shelves
nodes.rationale: Working products remain visible after assignment; exact-ID searches navigate to saved shelf cells. Search and selection inspect inventory without moving it.

nodes.label: Shelf Designer
nodes.rationale: Shelf previews remain unsaved until explicit commit; rows count upward from the ground. Shelf deletion is immediate but requires removal of regular and exception placements and resolution of pending editor changes.

nodes.label: Special Exceptions
nodes.rationale: Explicitly permits a product at multiple shelf locations. Placement, CSV registration, and catalog registration are separate operations tracked by staging status; changing a staged name reopens both registrations.

nodes.label: Switch / Combine Cells
nodes.rationale: Switch exchanges complete cell contents; combine empties a source into a destination while retaining destination contents. Each confirmed action uses one immediate SQLite transaction and preserves stock and original shelf-added timestamps.

nodes.label: Warehouse Shelf Mapper
nodes.rationale: A local Windows/Tkinter application maps products to irregular warehouse shelves; local SQLite avoids requiring Docker or a database server.

nodes.label: Web Location Sync
nodes.rationale: Imports KiotViet XLSX exports, compares complete location sets, resyncs comparable mismatches sequentially, and exports remaining mismatches. Local IDs absent from the export are not uploaded; location-only updates leave stock untouched.

nodes.label: Deprecated React/TypeScript web UI
nodes.rationale: Retained for reference with source, build script, and offline bundle; Tkinter is the supported interface and web rebuilding/optimization is outside the desktop refactor.

nodes.label: Local database backup
nodes.rationale: backups/ contains the backup from the one-time move out of the project root. Close the application before copying its database for another backup.

nodes.label: Background Excel comparison and resync verification
nodes.norm_label: background excel comparison and resync verification
nodes.rationale: Tab 7 compares Excel data in background workers and polls results onto the Tk thread. Location sets accept comma, semicolon, pipe, and newline separators. Missing export IDs cannot be compared/uploaded; verify resync using a fresh website export.

nodes.label: Immediate inventory save boundaries
nodes.rationale: Tab 2 inventory moves save immediately. Tab 5 confirmed switch/combine saves immediately and preserves quantities/timestamps. Shelf structure requires explicit commit, while exception placement and CSV/catalog registration are separate saves. Local assignment alone does not update KiotViet.

nodes.label: Incremental cache and widget refresh
nodes.rationale: StateActions reconciles only affected products and visible cells; database cache reload and widget refresh remain distinct to prevent duplicate redraws. Reuse rows/buttons when contents change, rebuild shelves for structure changes, and preserve selection, styling, and counts in partial refreshes.

nodes.label: Shift modifier state alignment
nodes.rationale: whole_mode, captured mouse Shift state, labels, click routing, action routing, and timer resets must stay aligned. Product lists cap displayed results at 750, so visible-queue transfers use narrowed displayed search results.

nodes.label: Shelf orientation and compact cell display
nodes.norm_label: shelf orientation and compact cell display
nodes.rationale: Layout arrays run from ground upward while renderers put the highest row first. Even-side rows display descending cell order without renumbering IDs. Compact Tab 2 cells retain numeric counts and gray/green/blue empty/occupied/selected styling during partial refresh.

nodes.label: Desktop tab callback and scan wiring
nodes.norm_label: desktop tab callback and scan wiring
nodes.rationale: WarehouseMapperApp._build_ui identifies active views and callbacks. Tab changes refresh the selected view and reset Shift mode; global barcode scans route to the active view. PrimalQueueView is active Tab 3 while ProductLookupView is retained older code.

nodes.label: Transactional inventory mutation ownership
nodes.rationale: Trace mutations from UI callback through action handler to database method and successful-write refresh. Transactional inventory changes belong in persistence rather than only tree rows or in-memory dictionaries.

nodes.label: Combined working and warehouse catalog
nodes.rationale: Display combines separate working and warehouse stores by product ID; queue names take precedence. Catalog-only transfer copies into the working list without deleting catalog rows, and pulling assigned/on-hand products back retains stock.

nodes.label: CSV reimport preservation
nodes.rationale: Reimport upserts product names while preserving placement, stock, historical assignment time, and IDs absent from later CSVs. Working and warehouse catalog imports remain separate.

nodes.label: Total queue, on-hand queue, and assigned locations
nodes.norm_label: total queue, on-hand queue, and assigned locations
nodes.rationale: Normal queue, on-hand, and assigned shelf states are distinct; multiple shelf locations require the explicit Special Exceptions workflow.

nodes.label: Explicit KiotViet browser updates
nodes.rationale: Web actions default to one selected product; the all-products option processes the loaded address sequentially, saving each product before opening the next and stopping at the first failed SKU to avoid advancing from an uncertain browser state.

nodes.label: Persistent on-hand batch
nodes.rationale: Moving products to on-hand saves quantities immediately in SQLite and survives restart. Ordinary assignment moves only the selected subset in one transaction, leaving other products on-hand.

nodes.label: Small Windows runtime launchers
nodes.rationale: Mapper and label executables launch root Python scripts using the existing project venv and source folders. Python edits take effect on the next launch; only launcher changes require rebuilding with utils/build_exe.py.

nodes.label: Scratch database manual verification
nodes.rationale: Launch with --db tmp/manual-check.db and sample inventory so manual checks do not modify working inventory.

nodes.label: Shift transfer shortcuts and reversal
nodes.rationale: Catalog and visible-queue direct transfers use stock 999; whole on-hand transfer retains quantities. Multi-result queue transfer requires a shared normalized five-character prefix and three Shift-clicks with a resetting three-second timeout. Reversal retains only the latest successful transfer in memory and is lost on application close.

nodes.label: Historical Vite development workflow
nodes.rationale: npm install and npm run dev run the historical web interface; Vite proxies /api to Python port 8000. warehouse_web.py starts the Python server and Node.js is needed to rebuild TypeScript.

nodes.label: Centralized location naming
nodes.rationale: mapper/core/common.py centralizes location rules; floor 1, side 1, shelf A, row 8, cell 10 produce L1-1A8-10.
